result.title: MOSAIC: Addressing Disproportionate Task-Modality Dependencies via Modality-Partitioned Gradient Routing
result.summary: In multi-task settings, combining multiple modalities allows task representations to draw on signals that a single modality alone would not capture. However, individual tasks may depend disproportionately on particular modalities, a structure that conventional fusion-based architectures do not model explicitly, instead enforcing a unified representation space. Consequently, a task's gradients can affect parameters tied to modalities it barely relies on, leaving features that compromise between competing demands. Although prior work has explored task-weighting and loss-balancing strategies, their effectiveness is limited by the absence of explicit modality separation, preventing models from optimising each modality according to its task-specific importance. To address these limitations, we propose MOSAIC (MOdality-Separated Architecture with Inter-modal Cross-attention), which preserves unimodal representations while enabling controlled interaction between them, and uses modality-specific losses to route gradients to their corresponding partitions. On the Corpus of Everyday Japanese Conversation (CEJC), MOSAIC improves average macro-F1 by 7.4 points across four tasks with a 72% reduction in backbone parameters relative to a fusion-based baseline. Our results demonstrate that modality partitioning yields consistent gains across tasks while requiring far fewer backbone parameters than a fusion-based design.

AI.brief_summary: 针对多任务多模态中某些任务过度依赖特定模态的问题，提出 MOSAIC：保留各模态独立表示并用受控跨模态 cross-attention 交互，同时以模态特定损失将梯度路由到对应分区；在日语会话语料四任务上 macro-F1 提升 7.4 点，主干参数减少 72%。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「保留单模态表示＋模态特定损失定向路由梯度」的做法，可供核查能否用于抑制 LVR 中的视觉旁路与信息坍缩、让视觉证据在内部状态中按任务需要保留，但原文并非推理期 latent 生成研究，需较多核查。
